name: Renderer Lifecycle
purpose: define renderer resolution, mount-instance cleanup and projector-boundary lifecycle semantics without making renderers authorities for domain data, authorization or application state
defaultRule: the default renderer is derived from the base projector id

destroy.scope: the single mount instance created by this mount call

mountSemantics.target: WebEngine-owned mount boundary for this projection instance; renderer must not mutate outside it
mountSemantics.projection: resolved projection input; renderer must not mutate it or become its authority
mountSemantics.context: runtime/page/identity/access context supplied by WebEngine; renderer must not treat it as mutable authority
mountSemantics.instanceIsolation: each mount call is independent even when the same renderer module is mounted multiple times
mountSemantics.cleanupRule: cleanup is bound to the mount result of one mount call; module-global destroy state is not canonical

values.loading: WebEngine is resolving, authorizing or mounting this projection generation and no terminal presentation state has been reached yet
values.ready: the current projection generation mounted successfully and has presentable output
values.empty: the current projection generation completed successfully but has no presentable output
values.denied: presentation was denied by the authorization/preflight path; renderer mount is not invoked for the denied generation
values.error: the current projection generation failed during resolution, loading or mount; the failure is isolated to this projector boundary
values.destroy: the current mount generation is being torn down and is terminal for that generation

rules: ready and empty are the only lifecycle outcomes a successful renderer mount may report
denied is owned by WebEngine authorization orchestration and is never returned by a renderer
error is produced by orchestration when an operation fails and is never used as a renderer success result
destroy is terminal for one mount generation even when the DOM boundary is later reused by a new generation
presentation state does not grant or revoke authorization
destroy -> loading is allowed only when the same DOM boundary is reused for a distinct new generation

when: page/surface owning the projection is destroyed
a superseded async mount resolves after a newer generation became current
ordering: mark the old generation as destroy
prevent the old generation from publishing further lifecycle state
invoke its returned destroy handle exactly once when present
remove or replace renderer-owned DOM within the mount target
release WebEngine references to the old generation
destroySemantics.failureRule: destroy failure must be contained to the old mount generation and must not resurrect or authorize it

asyncAndRaceSafety.generationRule: each mount attempt has a distinct generation identity owned by WebEngine
asyncAndRaceSafety.lateCompletionRule: a superseded async mount must not overwrite DOM or lifecycle state belonging to a newer generation
asyncAndRaceSafety.lateHandleRule: if a superseded mount later resolves with a destroy handle, WebEngine invokes that handle instead of publishing the stale result
asyncAndRaceSafety.cancellationRule: WebEngine may provide cancellation context such as an AbortSignal, but lifecycle correctness must not depend solely on renderer cooperation

failureIsolation.mountFailure: WebEngine catches renderer load/mount failure, contains it to the projector boundary and enters error
failureIsolation.partialSideEffects: if mount throws before returning a cleanup handle, the renderer is responsible for cleaning side effects it created outside the target; mutations inside the target may be discarded by WebEngine
failureIsolation.diagnostics: sensitive or verbose failure details must not be encoded into shared presentation attributes

rules: renderers are executable implementations outside the projector tree
a renderer may use WebGUI, S3D or native browser capabilities
a renderer does not become the authority for domain data, authorization, SiteTree or Actions
a renderer override must be explicit because the default path is derived
the same renderer module may be mounted concurrently in multiple independent projection instances
a module-global destroy() that cannot identify a mount instance is not the canonical cleanup model
WebEngine owns lifecycle orchestration and state publication
UI lifecycle state is not an authoritative backend security boundary
